big_picture_notes: Isaiah is a 66‑chapter prophetic anthology widely recognized as three major literary collections: Proto‑Isaiah (chs. 1–39, 8th‑century Assyrian crisis), Deutero‑Isaiah (chs. 40–55, 6th‑century Babylonian exile), and Trito‑Isaiah (chs. 56–66, post‑exilic restoration). The book is framed by 1:1 and unified by leitwort and motifs: 'Holy One of Israel,' blindness/deafness, covenant lawsuit (rîb), the Servant, and the promise of new creation. Genres range across oracle, narrative, woe, hymn, lament, and apocalypse. Structure is marked by inclusio, chiasm, catchwords, and historical setting shifts. For memorization, treat each small oracle or poetic unit as a scene; use clear markers (superscriptions, 'oracle' formulas, refrains, woe headings, Servant Songs) to segment.

stories.why_start_end_and_literary_glue: Chapters 1-12 introduce the whole book: a covenant lawsuit against Judah framed by judgment (ch.1) and a hymn of salvation (ch.12), an inclusio of 'judgment to joy.' Glue: the title 'Holy One of Israel,' the remnant theme, and the move from Assyrian judgment to messianic hope (the shoot from Jesse).

scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Formal title: author, genre ('vision'), scope (Judah/Jerusalem), reigns—sets historical frame.

scenes.scene_name: Covenant Lawsuit: Heavens and Earth Witness
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Rîb opening 'Hear, O heavens'; metaphor of ox/donkey knowing their master vs Israel's ignorance—charged irony.
Dense parallelism ('sinful nation… people laden with iniquity'); introduces title 'Holy One of Israel.'
Head‑to‑toe medical metaphor of the body politic—total corruption and untreated wounds.
Country desolate, cities burned; isolated hut similes; remnant motif averts Sodom‑like annihilation.
Shock vocatives; rhetorical questions reject mere appearance before God—empty ritual exposed.
List of hated festivals/offerings; God 'weary' of prayers—hands full of blood links worship to injustice.
Cascade of commands defining repentance: cease evil → learn good → seek justice (orphans/widow).

scenes.scene_name: Invitation to Reason: Scarlet and Snow
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Legal invitation; total cleansing similes (scarlet/snow); two‑ways conditional of blessing/curse.
Qinah 'How' dirge contrasts former fidelity with present corruption; dross/watered wine metaphors; social injustice named.
Solemn titles introduce refining imagery ('purge dross'); restoration to 'City of Righteousness' with new name.
Antithetical parallelism: Zion redeemed by justice vs rebels destroyed—binary outcome.

scenes.scene_name: Shame of Idolatry and Unquenchable Fire
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Oaks/gardens idolatry; withered oak and waterless garden similes; strong man as tinder—unquenchable end.

scenes.scene_name: The Mountain of the LORD's House
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The vision of the last days: all nations streaming to Zion, beating swords into plowshares.
The indictment of a people enriched yet bowing to the work of their own hands.

scenes.scene_name: The Day of the LORD Against the Proud
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The summons to hide in the dust, for the LORD alone will be exalted against all that is lofty.

scenes.scene_name: The Loftiness of Men Brought Low
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Judgment on cedars, mountains, towers, and ships — the pride of man humbled.

scenes.scene_name: Put No More Trust in Man
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Idols cast to moles and bats as men flee to caves — 'of what account' is mortal man?
God stripping Jerusalem of food, leaders, warriors, and counselors.
The collapse of order: youths as leaders and no one willing to govern the rubble.

scenes.scene_name: Like Sodom They Flaunt Their Sin
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Jerusalem fallen for defying the LORD; woe to the wicked, but well to the righteous.

scenes.scene_name: Grinding the Faces of the Poor
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The LORD rising to contend with the elders who have devoured His vineyard.
Judgment announced on the proud, prancing women of Zion.
The long inventory of stripped ornaments — anklets, veils, rings, and shawls.
Stench for fragrance, sackcloth for fine clothing, and the gates of Zion in mourning.
Seven women grasping one man (1), then the glorious Branch and the fruit of the land (2).
The cleansed remnant called holy, sheltered by a cloud and fire of glory.
The beloved's well-tended vineyard that yielded only sour grapes.

scenes.scene_name: What More Could I Have Done?
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The verdict to lay the vineyard waste — for the vineyard is Israel, yielding bloodshed instead of justice.

scenes.scene_name: Woe to Those Who Add House to House
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The first woe, against greed that leaves no room — desolate mansions and failed harvests.
The woe against those who chase strong drink and disregard the work of the LORD — exile follows.
The grave opening wide for Zion's revelers, while the LORD is exalted by His justice.

scenes.scene_name: Woe to Those Who Call Evil Good
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The woes against scoffers who drag sin along and invert good and evil, light and dark.

scenes.scene_name: Woe to the Wise in Their Own Eyes
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The woes against the self-wise and the bribe-takers who acquit the guilty.

scenes.scene_name: His Anger Is Not Turned Away
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Their decaying roots and the burning anger of the LORD whose hand is still upraised.

scenes.scene_name: A Banner for the Distant Nations
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The tireless invading army summoned from afar, roaring like a lion over a darkened land.
The throne-vision in the year Uzziah died: the seraphim's cry shaking the temple.
'Woe is me, I am ruined' — the unclean lips touched and atoned by the burning coal.
The commission to a people who hear but never understand, their hearts made calloused.

scenes.scene_name: The Holy Seed Is the Stump
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: 'How long?' — until the land is desolate, yet a holy seed remains in the felled stump.
The Syro-Ephraimite threat and Isaiah sent with his son to the trembling king.
The reassurance against the plot of Rezin and Pekah to install a puppet king.

scenes.scene_name: If You Do Not Stand Firm in Faith
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The oracle that the plot will fail — and the warning, 'you will not stand at all.'
The LORD's offer of a sign and Ahaz's false-piety refusal.
The sign of Immanuel given to the house of David, with the two dreaded kings soon laid waste.

scenes.scene_name: A Razor Hired from the Euphrates
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The coming of Assyria pictured as flies, bees, and a razor that shaves the land bare.
The desolation reducing the land to curds, honey, and thornbushes.
The prophet's son named 'swift to plunder' as a sign of Assyria's coming spoil.
Rejecting the gentle waters of Shiloah brings the Assyrian flood up to the neck — 'O Immanuel!'
The defiant taunt to the nations: every plan thwarted, for Immanuel — God is with us.
The charge to fear the LORD alone, who becomes both a sanctuary and a rock of offense.

scenes.scene_name: I Will Wait for the LORD
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Sealing the testimony among the disciples, trusting the God who hides His face.

scenes.scene_name: To the Law and to the Testimony
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The rejection of mediums for God's word, and the doom of those with no light of dawn.
The dawn over Galilee: a great light and multiplied joy for those in the shadow of death.

scenes.scene_name: Unto Us a Child Is Born
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The shattered yoke and the royal child — Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Prince of Peace — on David's throne.
Israel's prideful boast to rebuild grander after the message of judgment falls on Jacob.
Foes raised from east and west, with the recurring refrain of unrelenting anger.
The unrepentant people whose leaders mislead them, cut off in a single day.
Wickedness burning like fire and the land consuming itself in self-destruction.
The woe against oppressive decrees that prey on widows and orphans — what will they do on the day of reckoning?

scenes.scene_name: Assyria, the Rod of My Anger
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Assyria as the unwitting instrument of God's wrath, intent only on destruction.

scenes.scene_name: Will I Not Do to Jerusalem?
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The Assyrian's boast of conquered cities and his threat against Jerusalem and her idols.

scenes.scene_name: By the Strength of My Hand
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The arrogant self-praise of the conqueror who gathered the nations like abandoned eggs.
The rebuke of the tool that exalts itself over its wielder, and the wasting disease sent on Assyria.

scenes.scene_name: The Light of Israel a Fire
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The Holy One becoming a flame to devour Assyria's forest in a single day.
The surviving remnant truly leaning on the LORD, though destruction is decreed and overflowing.
Comfort to Zion: God's fury will soon turn, and the yoke will be broken from the neck.
The vivid march of the Assyrian army through the towns toward Jerusalem's hill.
The Lord lopping off the lofty branches with terrifying power.

scenes.scene_name: A Shoot from the Stump of Jesse
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The Branch on whom the sevenfold Spirit of the LORD rests, delighting in the fear of the LORD.
The righteous Judge of the poor who slays the wicked with the breath of His lips.
The peaceable kingdom where a child leads predators and the earth is full of the knowledge of the LORD.
The Root of Jesse drawing the nations, God's hand extended a second time to gather the exiles.
Ephraim and Judah reconciled and a new exodus-highway for the returning remnant.
The song of the redeemed: 'God is my salvation' — drawing water with joy from salvation's springs.
The closing doxology of Book I: proclaim His name, for great in Zion is the Holy One of Israel.

stories.why_start_end_and_literary_glue: Chapters 13-23 are a collection of 'oracle' (massa', 'burden') judgments against the foreign nations, each marked by the repeating oracle formula (13:1; 14:28; 15:1; 17:1; 19:1; 21:1,11,13; 22:1; 23:1). Start (13:1): the oracle concerning Babylon. End (23:18): Tyre's wealth consecrated to the LORD, completing the tour before ch.24's apocalyptic turn.

scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The superscription opening the oracles against the nations: the 'burden' against Babylon.
The banner raised and the LORD's sanctified warriors mustered from distant lands to execute His wrath.

scenes.scene_name: The Day of the LORD: Cosmic Dread
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: 'Wail, for the Day of the LORD is near' — melting hearts and a darkened sun, moon, and stars.
The LORD ending the pride of the arrogant, making man scarcer than gold, the heavens trembling.
The terror of the sack: the hunted fleeing, the captured slain, the city's horrors.
The pitiless Medes stirred up against the jewel of kingdoms, to be overthrown like Sodom.
Babylon never again inhabited, given over to desert beasts — 'her days will not be prolonged.'
The LORD choosing Israel again, the nations escorting them home, captives ruling their captors.
The taunt-song over the king of Babylon: the staff of the wicked broken at last.

scenes.scene_name: The Earth Breaks Out in Song
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: All the earth at rest, even Lebanon's cedars exulting that no woodcutter comes.
The shades of dead kings rising to greet the fallen tyrant on his bed of maggots.

scenes.scene_name: How You Have Fallen, O Day Star
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The proud boast 'I will ascend… I will make myself like the Most High.'
The fallen one stared at — 'is this the man who shook the earth?'
Denied honorable burial, dumped like a trampled carcass for destroying his own land.

scenes.scene_name: I Will Cut Off Babylon's Name
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The slaughter of his sons and the sweeping of Babylon away with the broom of destruction.
The sworn purpose to break Assyria, the outstretched hand none can turn back.
The oracle in the year Ahaz died: a viper from the snake's root, the Philistine remnant slain.
The wailing city and the answer to the envoys: Zion the refuge of His afflicted people.
The burden against Moab: Ar and Kir devastated, weeping at the high places, every head shaved.
The cry from Heshbon, the fleeing fugitives, the dried-up waters of Nimrim.

scenes.scene_name: The Waters of Dimon Full of Blood
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Moab carrying off its wealth, the outcry echoing to the borders, more judgment promised.
The plea from Sela to Zion, the daughters of Moab like fluttering birds at the Arnon.

scenes.scene_name: A Throne in the Tent of David
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The appeal to shelter the refugees, and the promise of a faithful Davidic judge.
Moab's pride answered by the withered vines of Sibmah trampled by the nations.

scenes.scene_name: I Weep for the Vines of Sibmah
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Joy removed from the orchard, the prophet's heart lamenting for Moab like a harp.

scenes.scene_name: In Three Years Moab's Splendor Gone
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Moab's vain prayer at the high place, and the dated word of contempt on her many people.
The burden against Damascus: the fortress gone from Ephraim, the sovereignty from Aram.
The fading splendor of Jacob, reduced to a few berries on a beaten olive tree.

scenes.scene_name: Men Will Look to Their Maker
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Turning eyes to the Holy One of Israel, away from hand-made altars and Asherahs.
The forgotten God of salvation, the exotic plantings whose harvest vanishes in pain.
The roaring nations rebuked and driven like chaff — 'before morning, they are no more.'

scenes.scene_name: Woe to the Land of Whirring Wings
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The oracle to the river-divided people of Cush and the banner raised on the mountains.
The LORD quietly watching, pruning the shoots, until gifts are brought to Zion.

scenes.scene_name: The LORD Rides on a Swift Cloud
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Egypt's idols trembling, Egyptian set against Egyptian, given to a harsh master.
The drying of Egypt's river, the withering reeds and rushes.
The collapse of Egypt's livelihoods — fishermen, flax-workers, and weavers dismayed.

scenes.scene_name: The Princes of Zoan Are Fools
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Pharaoh's wise counselors exposed as senseless, leading Egypt astray.
Egypt staggering like a drunkard, with nothing it can do, head or tail.
The fear of the LORD's uplifted hand, Judah a terror to Egypt.

scenes.scene_name: An Altar to the LORD in Egypt
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Five cities swearing allegiance, an altar and a savior for Egypt's oppressed.
The LORD striking and healing Egypt, who turns to Him in worship.
The highway of worship from Egypt to Assyria, and the threefold blessing with Israel.

scenes.scene_name: Naked and Barefoot for Three Years
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Isaiah's stripped sign against Egypt and Cush at the time of Sargon's attack on Ashdod.
The coming Assyrian exile of Egypt and Cush, dashing the coastland's misplaced hope.
The burden of a terror coming from the desert — 'Go up, O Elam! Lay siege, O Media!'
The prophet's labor-pang dread at the vision as the princes are roused to battle.
The posted lookout's watch and his cry of Babylon's fall and shattered idols.
The burden against Dumah: 'Morning has come, but also the night.'
The Dedanite caravans lodging in the thickets, the refugees met with water and food.
Within a year, the dated doom of the warriors of Kedar.
The city on the rooftops, its slain not fallen in battle — 'let me weep bitterly.'
The day of trampling and confusion, with Elam's quiver and chariots in the valleys.

scenes.scene_name: You Did Not Look to Its Maker
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Frantic defenses and a reservoir built, but no regard for the One who planned it long ago.

scenes.scene_name: Let Us Eat and Drink, for Tomorrow We Die
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Weeping called for but revelry chosen — a sin never to be atoned.
The steward who carved his own grand tomb, to be slung away into a wide land.
The office removed from Shebna and given to God's servant Eliakim, a father to Judah.

scenes.scene_name: The Key to the House of David
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The peg driven into a firm place with the key that opens and shuts (cited of Christ in Rev 3).
The overloaded peg sheared off — even the trusted office cannot bear all that hangs on it.
The burden against Tyre, the merchant of the nations, mourned by the ships of Tarshish.
The sea's barren lament and the call to flee to Tarshish.
The fall of the crown-bestowing city, devised to disgrace all the renowned of the earth.
The LORD's hand over the sea, giving the oppressed daughter of Sidon no rest.
The ruined Chaldean land as a warning, the ships of Tarshish wailing for a lost harbor.
Tyre forgotten seventy years, then her merchant-profits set apart as holy to the LORD.

stories.why_start_end_and_literary_glue: Chapters 24-27, the 'Isaiah Apocalypse': cosmic, universal judgment on the whole earth followed by resurrection, the swallowing up of death, and the eschatological banquet on Zion. Start (24:1): 'Behold, the LORD lays waste the earth.' End (27:13): the great trumpet gathering the scattered to worship on the holy mountain. Glue: world-scale de-creation and the 'city' (chaos) versus Zion motif.

scenes.scene_name: The LORD Lays Waste the Earth
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The apocalypse opens: the whole earth scattered and plundered, leveling every social rank.

scenes.scene_name: A Curse Has Consumed the Earth
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The mourning, withering world, defiled by breaking the everlasting covenant, with only a few left.
The end of all merrymaking — the wine dried up, the harp silent, strong drink turned bitter.

scenes.scene_name: The City of Chaos Is Shattered
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The ruined 'city of chaos,' its gate rubble, all joy exiled from the land.
The gleaned remnant raising songs from west and east to the majesty of the LORD.
The prophet's 'woe is me' amid treachery, the inescapable terrors and opened windows of heaven.

scenes.scene_name: The Earth Staggers Like a Drunkard
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The earth split and swaying under the weight of its rebellion, fallen never to rise.

scenes.scene_name: The LORD Will Reign on Mount Zion
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The host of heaven and kings imprisoned, the sun and moon ashamed before the reigning LORD.
The hymn of praise for the long-formed plans that made the ruthless city a heap of rubble.
God a stronghold and shade in distress, silencing the song of the ruthless.

scenes.scene_name: He Will Swallow Up Death Forever
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The lavish banquet on the mountain where the shroud over the nations is removed and death destroyed.

scenes.scene_name: This Is Our God; We Have Waited
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The rejoicing of the saved as the LORD's hand rests on Zion and Moab is trampled.
The high-walled fortress of Moab cast down into the dust.
The song of the strong city: the steadfast mind kept in peace, trusting the Rock eternal.
The high city humbled under the feet of the poor, the path of the righteous made level.

scenes.scene_name: My Soul Longs for You in the Night
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Waiting on the LORD whose judgments teach the world righteousness, though grace is wasted on the wicked.

scenes.scene_name: You Will Establish Peace for Us
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The unseen upraised hand, the peace God works, and the confession of His name alone.
The dead tyrants who will not rise, the enlarged nation, the quiet prayer poured out under discipline.
The labor that gave birth only to wind (17-18) answered by the resurrection promise — 'awake and sing, you who dwell in the dust' (19).

scenes.scene_name: Hide Until the Wrath Has Passed
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The people sheltered while the LORD comes from His dwelling to punish the earth's bloodshed.
The dragon of the sea judged (1), and the LORD's well-watered vineyard He guards night and day (2-5).
Israel budding to fill the world with fruit, struck more gently than her oppressors.
Exile as God's measured contention, its fruit the smashing of every altar and Asherah.
The deserted city stripped bare, whose Maker shows no favor to the senseless.
The threshing from Euphrates to Egypt and the trumpet gathering the exiles to worship on the holy mountain.

stories.why_start_end_and_literary_glue: Chapters 28-33 are a series of 'Woe' (hoy) oracles against the drunkards of Ephraim, complacent Ariel/Jerusalem, and the leaders who trust in an Egyptian alliance rather than the LORD. Start (28:1): 'Woe to the proud crown of the drunkards of Ephraim.' End (33:24): Zion forgiven, the LORD her king and judge. Glue: the recurring 'hoy' and the contrast of false security with trust in the cornerstone in Zion (28:16).

scenes.scene_name: Woe to the Drunkards of Ephraim
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The fading-flower crown of Samaria's drunkards to be smashed by the LORD's mighty storm.

scenes.scene_name: Priests and Prophets Reel from Wine
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The LORD a crown to the remnant (5-6), set against the vomit-covered tables of befuddled leaders (7-8).

scenes.scene_name: Order on Order, Line on Line
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The mocking of God's teaching as fit only for infants, in stammering syllables.

scenes.scene_name: This Is the Place of Rest
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The offered rest refused, so the word becomes a snare that trips them backward.
The Jerusalem scoffers boasting that lies and falsehood will shelter them from the scourge.
The precious sure foundation laid in Zion — 'the one who believes will never be shaken.'
The annulled pact with Sheol and the relentless scourge that brings sheer terror.
The too-short bed, the LORD rising to do His alien task of judgment, the decreed destruction.
God instructing the farmer in his seasons and varied sowing as a picture of His wise dealings.
Different grains threshed by different means — the LORD excellent in wisdom.
The siege of David's city, brought so low its voice whispers from the dust.

scenes.scene_name: Like a Dream in the Night
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Ariel's many foes turned to dust, the besieging nations vanishing like a hungry man's dream.
Blindness and stupor poured out, the eyes of the prophets and seers covered.
The whole vision become like sealed words none can read.
Worship reduced to man-made rules, so the wisdom of the wise will perish (cited by Jesus).
Woe to those who hide plans from God, turning things upside down as if the clay could deny its maker.
The coming reversal: Lebanon an orchard, the blind seeing, the humble increasing their joy.
The cutting-down of mockers and those who deprive the innocent of justice at the gate.

scenes.scene_name: Jacob Will No Longer Be Ashamed
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The redeemed house of Jacob honoring God's name, the wayward coming to understanding.
The alliance with Egypt formed against God's will — Pharaoh's protection turned to shame.
The treasure-laden caravan to a useless Egypt, whose help is empty.
The witness inscribed against a people who tell the seers to silence the Holy One of Israel.

scenes.scene_name: Like a Breach About to Fail
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The rejected message bringing sudden collapse, shattered like a potter's jar.
'In repentance and rest you would be saved' — refused for swift horses and a faster pursuit.

scenes.scene_name: The LORD Longs to Be Gracious
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The just God waiting to show compassion — 'blessed are all who wait for Him.'

scenes.scene_name: This Is the Way; Walk in It
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The unhidden Teacher and the guiding voice, leading them to cast away their idols.

scenes.scene_name: He Heals the Wounds He Inflicted
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Rain and rich harvests, sevenfold light on the day the LORD binds up His people's brokenness.

scenes.scene_name: The Name of the LORD Comes from Afar
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The advancing wrath with fury-filled lips and a breath like a neck-high torrent.
The festival song and the LORD's majestic arm striking Assyria with His scepter.
Each punishing stroke set to music, the deep funeral pyre kindled by the breath of the LORD.

scenes.scene_name: Woe to Those Who Go Down to Egypt
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Trusting horses and chariots, not the Holy One — 'the Egyptians are men, not God.'
The LORD as a fearless lion and a sheltering bird who will protect and deliver Jerusalem.

scenes.scene_name: Return to the One You Rebelled Against
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The call to repent and reject the silver and gold idols their own hands made.

scenes.scene_name: Assyria Will Fall, Not by Man's Sword
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The collapse of Assyria before the LORD whose fire is in Zion.

scenes.scene_name: A King Will Reign in Righteousness
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The coming just reign, each ruler a shelter, opening the eyes and ears of the people.

scenes.scene_name: No Longer a Fool Called Noble
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The clear distinction restored between the scoundrel's destructive plots and the noble man's honorable plans.
The warning to the secure women of a failed harvest — 'strip yourselves bare and put on sackcloth.'
Mourning over thorn-overgrown fields and the abandoned, donkey-roamed city.

scenes.scene_name: Until the Spirit Is Poured Out
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The desert turned orchard, justice dwelling in the wilderness, the work of righteousness peace.
God's people secure, blessed are those who sow beside abundant waters.
The treacherous one finally betrayed; the prayer 'be our strength every morning.'

scenes.scene_name: The Fear of the LORD Is Zion's Treasure
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The exalted LORD filling Zion with justice, a sure foundation of salvation and wisdom.
The broken treaty, the deserted highways, the mourning, decaying land.
The LORD rising to be exalted, the chaff-conceived plans consumed like thorns, and the summons to far and near to acknowledge His might.

scenes.scene_name: Who Can Dwell with Consuming Fire?
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The terror of the sinners in Zion answered by the one who walks righteously and dwells on the heights.
Eyes that will see the King and a land afar, the former terror of the tax-counter gone.
Zion the unwandering tent, the LORD her Judge, lawgiver, and King who will save.

scenes.scene_name: No Resident Will Say 'I Am Sick'
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The lame carrying off plunder and the forgiven people of Zion.

stories.why_start_end_and_literary_glue: Chapters 34-35 form a hinge diptych: the LORD's furious judgment on the nations (Edom as type, ch.34) set against the blossoming desert and the Highway of Holiness on which the redeemed return to Zion (ch.35). Start (34:1): 'Come near, you nations, and listen.' End (35:10): 'the ransomed of the LORD will return... with everlasting joy.' Glue: the antithesis of wilderness-curse and wilderness-bloom.

scenes.scene_name: The LORD Is Angry with All Nations
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The summons to the nations to hear the universal judgment as the skies are rolled up like a scroll.
The LORD's blood-bathed sword descending on Edom — a day of vengeance for the cause of Zion.

scenes.scene_name: A Line of Chaos Over Edom
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Edom's streams turned to pitch, given to owls and ravens, measured for desolation.
The thorn-overgrown fortresses become the lair of desert creatures and the night-bird.
God's sure word allotting the desolate land to the wild creatures forever.

scenes.scene_name: The Desert Will Blossom Like a Rose
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The wilderness rejoicing and blooming, beholding the glory of the LORD.
The charge to strengthen weak hands — 'your God will come with vengeance… to save you.'

scenes.scene_name: The Blind Will See, the Lame Will Leap
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The healing of the world: opened eyes, leaping lame, and waters gushing in the desert.
The highway on which the ransomed of the LORD return to Zion with everlasting joy.

stories.why_start_end_and_literary_glue: Chapters 36-39 are the prose historical bridge (paralleling 2 Kings 18-20): Sennacherib's siege and blasphemy, Hezekiah's prayer and the angel's deliverance, Hezekiah's illness and recovery, and the fateful visit of the Babylonian envoys that foreshadows the exile. Start (36:1): Sennacherib's invasion. End (39:8): the word that all will be carried to Babylon, setting up the Book of Comfort. Glue: trust versus the threat of empire, pivoting from Assyria to Babylon.

scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The Assyrian capture of Judah's cities and the Rabshakeh sent to Jerusalem's wall.

scenes.scene_name: A Splintered Reed of a Staff
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The Rabshakeh's taunt against trusting Egypt or the LORD whose altars Hezekiah removed.

scenes.scene_name: Was It Apart from the LORD?
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The mocking wager and the claim that the LORD Himself sent Assyria against the land.
The officials' plea answered by the Rabshakeh's deliberate Hebrew threat to the people.

scenes.scene_name: Do Not Let Hezekiah Deceive You
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The loud call over the wall against trusting Hezekiah's promise of deliverance.
The offer of vine and fig tree before deportation to 'a land like your own.'

scenes.scene_name: How Can the LORD Deliver Jerusalem?
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The blasphemous boast that no nation's god has rescued it from Assyria.
Hezekiah's command of silence, and the torn-clothed officials reporting back.

scenes.scene_name: Lift Up a Prayer for the Remnant
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Hezekiah in sackcloth sending to Isaiah on this day of distress and disgrace.
Isaiah's answer: a spirit put in the Assyrian to send him home to fall by the sword.

scenes.scene_name: Do Not Let Your God Deceive You
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Sennacherib's renewed message threatening that no god has spared any land.
The roll-call of conquered nations and their powerless gods.
Hezekiah laying the letter before the LORD enthroned above the cherubim, the only God.

scenes.scene_name: That All May Know You Alone Are God
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The prayer owning Assyria's conquests yet pleading for a salvation that proves the LORD alone is God.

scenes.scene_name: The Virgin Daughter of Zion Despises You
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Isaiah's oracle: Zion mocks the blasphemer who taunted the Holy One of Israel.
The Assyrian's recounted boast of cutting Lebanon's cedars and drying Egypt's streams.
The LORD's word that He decreed Assyria's conquests, its peoples like rooftop grass.
The God who knows the king's raging and will lead him back the way he came.
The sign of self-sown harvests and the surviving remnant rooting from Mount Zion.
The promise that Assyria will not enter or besiege Jerusalem, saved for David's sake.
185,000 slain in a night, Sennacherib's withdrawal and his murder in his god's temple.
Hezekiah's mortal illness and his weeping prayer recalling his faithful walk.
The LORD's answer through Isaiah: prayer heard, life extended, the city delivered.

scenes.scene_name: The Shadow Goes Back Ten Steps
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The sign on the stairway of Ahaz, the sunlight reversing its descent.
Hezekiah's writing of his despair at being cut off in the prime of life.

scenes.scene_name: Like a Lion He Breaks My Bones
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The imagery of a tent struck and a weaver's web cut — 'O Lord… be my security.'

scenes.scene_name: You Cast My Sins Behind Your Back
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The restored king's testimony that God's love delivered him from the pit of oblivion.
Sheol cannot praise God, but the living tell His faithfulness with songs in His house.
Isaiah's remedy for the boil and Hezekiah's question about the sign.
Hezekiah gladly showing the Babylonian envoys all his treasures and armory.
Isaiah's questioning, and Hezekiah's admission that he hid nothing.
The prophecy of exile to Babylon, met by Hezekiah's complacent 'the word… is good.'

stories.why_start_end_and_literary_glue: Chapters 40-55: the abrupt turn from judgment to comfort for the exiles, dominated by the new exodus, the polemics against idols, the Creator-Redeemer, and the four Servant Songs (42:1-9; 49:1-7; 50:4-11; 52:13-53:12). Start (40:1): 'Comfort, comfort My people.' End (55:13): the cypress for the thorn, an everlasting sign. Glue: 'comfort,' the incomparable Creator, and the Servant who brings justice and bears sin.

scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The Book of Comfort opens: Jerusalem's warfare ended and her iniquity pardoned.

scenes.scene_name: Prepare the Way for the LORD
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The wilderness voice leveling every valley and mountain so the glory of the LORD is revealed.

scenes.scene_name: The Word of Our God Stands Forever
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: All flesh is grass that withers, but God's word endures.

scenes.scene_name: He Tends His Flock Like a Shepherd
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Zion the herald — 'Here is your God!' — coming with might yet carrying the lambs close to His heart.
The incomparable Creator who needs no counselor.

scenes.scene_name: The Nations Are a Drop in a Bucket
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: All nations as nothing before Him, the islands like fine dust.

scenes.scene_name: To Whom Will You Liken God?
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The folly of comparing the LORD to a craftsman's gold-overlaid idol.

scenes.scene_name: Enthroned Above the Circle of the Earth
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The Creator who stretches the heavens like a tent and brings princes to nothing.

scenes.scene_name: He Calls Each Star by Name
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The Holy One leading forth the starry host, not one missing.

scenes.scene_name: The Everlasting God Does Not Grow Weary
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The answer to Jacob's complaint that his way is hidden — the tireless Creator of the ends of the earth.

scenes.scene_name: They Will Mount Up with Wings Like Eagles
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The promise that those who wait on the LORD renew their strength.

scenes.scene_name: I, the First and the Last
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The trial of the nations: who roused the conqueror from the east? — 'I, the LORD… I am He.'
The trembling islands propping up their idols against the coming judgment.

scenes.scene_name: Do Not Fear, for I Am with You
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Israel the chosen servant, upheld by God's righteous right hand.

scenes.scene_name: All Who Rage Against You Will Be Ashamed
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The vanishing of Israel's foes and the hand that takes hold of her right hand.

scenes.scene_name: You Worm Jacob, I Will Help You
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The Redeemer making lowly Israel a sharp threshing sledge to crush the mountains.
The poor given water, the desert planted, that all may know the Holy One has done it.
The challenge to the idols to foretell — 'you are nothing and your work is of no value.'

scenes.scene_name: A Herald of Good News to Zion
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The one raised from the north, and the LORD the first to announce it to Jerusalem.
No counselor among the idols, whose works are empty as the wind.
The first Servant Song: the Spirit-endowed One who brings justice to the nations — 'a bruised reed He will not break.'
The Creator appointing the Servant as a covenant to open blind eyes and free prisoners.

scenes.scene_name: I Will Not Yield My Glory
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The LORD declaring new things before they spring forth.

scenes.scene_name: Sing to the LORD a New Song
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The summons to the ends of the earth, the desert, and the islands to praise.
The long-silent LORD now crying out as a warrior to lay waste His enemies.
Guiding the blind on unfamiliar paths, turning darkness to light, while idolaters are shamed.

scenes.scene_name: Who Is Blind but My Servant?
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The rebuke of the deaf and blind servant who sees much yet keeps no watch.
The magnified law against a trapped, imprisoned people with none to rescue them.

scenes.scene_name: He Poured Out His Furious Anger
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Israel handed over for spoil because of sin, consumed by flames it would not understand.

scenes.scene_name: I Have Redeemed You; You Are Mine
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: 'When you pass through the waters, I will be with you' — preserved through flood and fire.

scenes.scene_name: I Give Egypt for Your Ransom
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Israel precious and honored, nations given in exchange for her life.

scenes.scene_name: Gathered from the Ends of the Earth
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The sons and daughters called by His name brought from every direction.
The blind-and-deaf people summoned to testify that before God no other was formed.

scenes.scene_name: There Is No Savior but Me
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The eternal LORD from whose hand none can deliver, whose acts none can reverse.
The Redeemer and King bringing down the Chaldeans for His people's sake.

scenes.scene_name: Behold, I Am Doing a New Thing
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The God of the Red Sea now making a way in the wilderness and streams in the desert.

scenes.scene_name: The People I Formed for Myself
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Water in the desert for His chosen, who will declare His praise.

scenes.scene_name: You Have Burdened Me with Your Sins
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Israel weary of God, bringing not sacrifices but iniquities.
The God who erases sins for His own sake, against a people whose first father sinned.

scenes.scene_name: I Will Pour Out My Spirit
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Comfort to Jeshurun: the Spirit poured on offspring who will claim the LORD's name.
'I am the first and the last' — the only God, with His people as witnesses.

scenes.scene_name: All Makers of Idols Are Nothing
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The worthless idols and their makers brought to shame.
The labor of forging and carving a god from a tree.

scenes.scene_name: He Worships a Block of Wood
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Half the wood burned for warmth and bread, the rest made into a god — 'Save me!'
The blinded idolater who cannot see the lie in his right hand.

scenes.scene_name: I Have Blotted Out Your Transgressions
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The call to return to the Redeemer, with heaven and earth bidden to sing for joy.
The Maker who confounds diviners and confirms His servant's word of restoration.
The naming of Cyrus, who will say of Jerusalem and the temple, 'Be rebuilt.'
The LORD grasping Cyrus's hand to subdue nations and open gates, giving him the treasures of darkness.

scenes.scene_name: I Form Light and Create Darkness
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The naming of the unknowing Cyrus for Jacob's sake, that all may know the LORD does all things.

scenes.scene_name: Woe to Him Who Quarrels with His Maker
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Heavens raining righteousness, and the folly of the clay arguing with the potter.

scenes.scene_name: I Will Raise Up Cyrus in Righteousness
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The Maker of earth and man raising Cyrus to rebuild His city and free the exiles.
The nations bowing in confession, idol-makers shamed, but Israel saved everlastingly.

scenes.scene_name: I Did Not Create It to Be Empty
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The Creator who formed the earth to be inhabited and speaks not in secret.

scenes.scene_name: Turn to Me and Be Saved
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The summons to the fugitive nations: 'Turn to Me and be saved, all the ends of the earth.'
The sworn word (quoted by Paul) that every knee will bow and every tongue swear allegiance.
The Babylonian gods carted off as burdens, going into captivity themselves.

scenes.scene_name: I Will Carry You When You Turn Gray
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The LORD who has borne Israel from the womb and will sustain her to old age.

scenes.scene_name: They Carry a God That Cannot Answer
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The contrast of the incomparable LORD with the silent, immovable idol.

scenes.scene_name: I Declare the End from the Beginning
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The God whose purpose stands and whose good pleasure is always accomplished.

scenes.scene_name: I Am Bringing My Righteousness Near
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The bird of prey summoned from the east, salvation granted to Zion.

scenes.scene_name: Sit in the Dust, O Daughter of Babylon
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The proud queen-city humbled to grind flour, her nakedness exposed in vengeance.
Babylon, who showed God's people no mercy, sent into silent darkness.

scenes.scene_name: Loss of Children and Widowhood in a Day
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The self-secure boaster — 'I am, and there is none besides me' — overtaken in a moment.
Disaster she cannot charm away falling suddenly on her wicked confidence.
The star-gazing counselors who cannot save themselves from the flame.

scenes.scene_name: You Swear by the LORD, but Not in Truth
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The hollow piety of the house of Jacob who lean on God in name only.

scenes.scene_name: I Foretold It, Lest You Credit Your Idols
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The former things announced in advance because Israel is stubborn as iron and bronze.
God revealing fresh things to a people deceitful and called a rebel from birth.
God restraining wrath for His name's sake, refining Israel for His own glory.
'I am the first and I am the last' — the Creator at whose summons all things stand.

scenes.scene_name: The LORD's Chosen Ally Against Babylon
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The called conqueror who will succeed, with the Servant sent by the Lord GOD and His Spirit.

scenes.scene_name: Your Peace Would Have Been Like a River
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The Redeemer-Teacher's lament for the peace forfeited by disobedience.
The shout of redemption and water from the rock — 'no peace for the wicked.'
The second Servant Song: a mouth like a sharp sword, hidden in God's quiver — 'You are My Servant.'

scenes.scene_name: A Light to the Ends of the Earth
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Labor seemingly in vain, yet the Servant given to bring salvation to all nations.
The despised Servant honored by kings, appointed a covenant to free the prisoners.

scenes.scene_name: They Will Not Hunger or Thirst
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The compassionate Shepherd guiding the returning exiles beside springs of water.

scenes.scene_name: Can a Woman Forget Her Nursing Child?
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Heaven's song of comfort answering Zion's 'the LORD has forgotten me' — 'I will not forget you.'

scenes.scene_name: Inscribed on the Palms of My Hands
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Zion's walls ever before God, her builders returning, her children worn like jewels.
The once-bereaved Zion astonished at her crowding children.

scenes.scene_name: Kings Will Be Your Foster Fathers
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The nations bringing Zion's sons and daughters, bowing before her — none who hope in Him are shamed.

scenes.scene_name: I Will Contend with Those Who Contend with You
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The captives reclaimed from the tyrant, that all may know the LORD is Savior and Redeemer.

scenes.scene_name: Where Is Your Mother's Certificate of Divorce?
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Israel sold for her own sins, not cast off — and God's hand is not too short to redeem.

scenes.scene_name: I Offered My Back to Those Who Struck Me
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The Servant with the disciple's tongue, unrebellious under scorn and spitting.

scenes.scene_name: I Have Set My Face Like Flint
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The vindicated Servant who fears no accuser, for the Lord GOD helps Him.

scenes.scene_name: Trust in the Name of the LORD
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The call to the God-fearer to lean on God in darkness, against those who walk by their own firebrands.

scenes.scene_name: Look to the Rock from Which You Were Cut
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The pursuers of righteousness pointed to Abraham and Sarah, and to the comfort of Zion's ruins made like Eden.
A law and justice going out as a light to the nations, outlasting the wearing-out heavens.

scenes.scene_name: Do Not Fear the Scorn of Men
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Those with God's law in their hearts told not to dread insults that the moth will devour.

scenes.scene_name: Awake, O Arm of the LORD
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The plea to the arm that cut Rahab and dried the sea, that the redeemed return to Zion with singing.

scenes.scene_name: I Am He Who Comforts You
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Why fear mortal man and forget the LORD your Maker who stretched out the heavens?

scenes.scene_name: I Have Put My Words in Your Mouth
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The captive soon freed, sheltered in the shadow of God's hand — 'You are My people.'
Jerusalem rousing from the cup of God's fury, her fainting sons lying in the streets.

scenes.scene_name: I Have Removed the Cup from Your Hand
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The cup of staggering taken from Zion and placed in the hands of her tormentors.

scenes.scene_name: Awake, Clothe Yourself with Strength, O Zion
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The captive Daughter of Zion called to shake off her dust and put on garments of splendor.

scenes.scene_name: Sold for Nothing, Redeemed Without Money
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Israel's oppression in Egypt and Assyria, leading to the day she knows His name.
The herald on the mountains proclaiming 'Your God reigns!' as the watchmen shout for joy.

scenes.scene_name: The LORD Has Bared His Holy Arm
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The ruins of Jerusalem breaking into song as all the earth sees God's salvation.
The summons to leave Babylon in purity, the LORD as both vanguard and rear guard.
The fourth Servant Song opens: the marred Servant raised high, sprinkling many nations and silencing kings.
Who has believed the message? — the Servant without majesty, a man of sorrows acquainted with grief.
The heart of the gospel: He bore our sorrows, crushed for our iniquities — 'by His stripes we are healed.'

scenes.scene_name: Led Like a Lamb to the Slaughter
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The silent, oppressed Servant cut off from the living, assigned a grave with the wicked though sinless.
The LORD's will to crush Him as a guilt offering, who then sees His offspring and bears the sin of many.

scenes.scene_name: Shout for Joy, O Barren Woman
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The desolate woman with more children than the married, called to enlarge her tent.
The shame of widowhood forgotten as the Redeemer calls back His wounded wife.

scenes.scene_name: With Everlasting Kindness I Will Gather You
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: A brief forsaking swallowed up by everlasting compassion.

scenes.scene_name: My Covenant of Peace Will Not Be Broken
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: As sure as the oath to Noah: though mountains depart, God's devotion will not.
The storm-lashed city rebuilt in jewels, all her sons taught by the LORD.

scenes.scene_name: No Weapon Formed Against You Will Prosper
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Established in righteousness, far from terror — the heritage of the servants of the LORD.

scenes.scene_name: Come, All You Who Are Thirsty
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The free invitation to the waters and to the everlasting covenant of devotion promised to David.
Nations unknown running to Israel because the Holy One has bestowed glory on her.

scenes.scene_name: Seek the LORD While He May Be Found
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The call to the wicked to forsake his way and return for free pardon.

scenes.scene_name: My Thoughts Are Not Your Thoughts
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: God's ways as high above ours as the heavens above the earth.

scenes.scene_name: My Word Will Not Return Empty
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Like rain and snow, God's word accomplishes what He pleases.

scenes.scene_name: You Will Go Out with Joy
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The closing inclusio: mountains singing, the cypress for the thorn, an everlasting sign for the LORD.

stories.why_start_end_and_literary_glue: Chapters 56-66 address the post-exilic community: the inclusion of foreigners, corrupt leaders, true versus false fasting and worship, and the climactic promise of new heavens and a new earth. Start (56:1): 'Keep justice and do righteousness, for My salvation is near.' End (66:24): the solemn final image of judgment outside the new creation. Glue: a chiasm centered on ch.60-62 (Zion's light and the Anointed) and the resolution of judgment/salvation and inclusion/exclusion.

scenes.scene_name: Maintain Justice; My Salvation Is Near
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Trito-Isaiah opens with the call to do right and keep the Sabbath as salvation draws near.

scenes.scene_name: A Name Better Than Sons and Daughters
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The eunuch who keeps God's covenant given an everlasting name in His house.

scenes.scene_name: A House of Prayer for All Nations
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The foreigners joined to the LORD welcomed to His holy mountain and altar.
The mute-dog shepherds without discernment, each seeking his own gain and drink.
The devout taken away from evil, entering into peace in death.
The indictment of idolaters who burn with lust and slaughter their children.

scenes.scene_name: Your Bed on a Lofty Hill
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The smooth-stone idols and the bed of spiritual adultery set up behind the door.

scenes.scene_name: You Went to Molech with Oil
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The wearying journeys of idolatry descending even to Sheol.

scenes.scene_name: He Who Seeks Refuge in Me Will Inherit the Land
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The long-silent God exposing their worthless idols, against the one who takes refuge in Him.
The high and holy One who inhabits eternity yet revives the heart of the lowly.

scenes.scene_name: Peace to Those Far and Near
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: God striking the greedy yet promising to heal and restore comfort to the mourners.
The wicked like the storm-tossed sea that cannot be still.

scenes.scene_name: Declare to My People Their Sin
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The trumpet-cry against a people who seek God daily yet do injustice.

scenes.scene_name: The Fast That God Has Not Chosen
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Fasting paired with oppression and strife, a mere bowing of the head.
To loose the chains of wickedness, feed the hungry, and shelter the homeless.

scenes.scene_name: Then Your Light Will Break Forth
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The promise of light, healing, and answered prayer for those who remove the yoke.
The well-watered garden and the rebuilt ancient ruins for those who give themselves to the afflicted.

scenes.scene_name: If You Call the Sabbath a Delight
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The promise of riding on the heights for those who honor the LORD's holy day.
The arm of the LORD not too short, but sin has hidden His face.

scenes.scene_name: They Hatch the Eggs of Vipers
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The portrait of pervasive deceit and violence that can clothe no one.

scenes.scene_name: The Way of Peace They Have Not Known
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Feet swift to shed blood, leaving ruin in their crooked paths.
The communal confession: hoping for light but walking in gloom.
The acknowledged transgressions that turn justice away and let truth stumble.
God amazed that no one intercedes, putting on the breastplate of righteousness and helmet of salvation.
Recompense to His enemies, that all may fear His name from east to west.

scenes.scene_name: The Redeemer Will Come to Zion
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The covenant promise that His Spirit and words will never depart from His people.

scenes.scene_name: Arise, Shine, for Your Light Has Come
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The glory of the LORD rising on Zion, nations and kings coming to her dawn.

scenes.scene_name: The Wealth of Nations Will Come to You
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Sons and daughters returning, the riches of the sea brought to a radiant Zion.
The caravans of camels and flocks of Kedar adorning God's glorious house.

scenes.scene_name: The Ships of Tarshish in the Lead
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The islands bringing Zion's children from afar with silver and gold.

scenes.scene_name: Your Gates Will Always Stand Open
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Foreigners rebuilding her walls, the wealth of nations led in through ever-open gates.
The glory of Lebanon adorning the sanctuary, oppressors' sons bowing at Zion's feet.
The once-forsaken city made a joy from age to age, knowing the LORD as Savior.

scenes.scene_name: Walls Called Salvation, Gates Called Praise
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Gold for bronze, peace as governor, violence heard no more in the land.
No more sun or moon needed, for the LORD is Zion's unsetting light.
A wholly righteous people, the least becoming a mighty nation in its time.

scenes.scene_name: The Spirit of the Lord GOD Is on Me
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The anointed One (read by Jesus in Nazareth) preaching good news and giving a crown of beauty for ashes.

scenes.scene_name: They Will Rebuild the Ancient Ruins
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The renewed cities and strangers tending the flocks of God's people.
God's people named His priests, receiving a double portion for their shame.
The LORD who loves justice blessing their descendants among the nations.
The joyful soul clothed like a bride, as righteousness springs up before all nations.

scenes.scene_name: A New Name the LORD Will Bestow
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: For Zion's sake the unsilenced cry until her righteousness shines like a torch.
No longer Forsaken or Desolate, but God's delight and bride.
The intercessors giving God no rest until He makes Jerusalem the praise of the earth.

scenes.scene_name: Never Again Given to Your Enemies
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The sworn promise that the harvesters will eat and drink in His holy courts.
The highway prepared and the banner raised — Zion called the Redeemed of the LORD.
The crimson-robed Warrior treading the winepress of vengeance alone.

scenes.scene_name: The Day of Vengeance in My Heart
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: God's own arm bringing salvation when no one was found to help.

scenes.scene_name: The Angel of His Presence Saved Them
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The recital of God's compassion, afflicted in His people's affliction, carrying them of old.
The rebellion that turned God to enemy, and the remembering of the days of Moses.
The glorious arm leading Israel through the depths to win Himself an everlasting name.
The plea for God to look down — 'our Redeemer from Everlasting is Your name.'

scenes.scene_name: Our Enemies Have Trampled Your Sanctuary
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The lament that God's holy place is profaned, His people like those never His.

scenes.scene_name: Oh, That You Would Rend the Heavens
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The cry for God to come down so the mountains quake at His presence.

scenes.scene_name: No Eye Has Seen Any God Besides You
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The God who acts for those who wait, against whom they have sinned.

scenes.scene_name: All Our Righteous Acts Are Like Filthy Rags
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The confession of withering corruption and a hidden divine face.

scenes.scene_name: We Are the Clay, You the Potter
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The appeal to the Father-Potter not to remember iniquity forever.
The ruined temple and cities, with the cry, 'Will You keep silent?'

scenes.scene_name: I Held Out My Hands All Day Long
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: God found by those who did not seek Him, His hands stretched to an obstinate people.
The provoking idolaters who say 'I am holier than you,' a fire burning all day.

scenes.scene_name: I Will Repay into Their Laps
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The written record of judgment for their sins and their fathers'.

scenes.scene_name: Do Not Destroy It; There Is a Blessing
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The new wine in the cluster — God preserving His servants to possess His mountains.
Judgment on those who forsake the LORD to set a table for Fortune and Destiny.

scenes.scene_name: My Servants Will Eat, but You Will Hunger
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The great divide between the rejoicing servants and the shamed rebels.
A new name for the servants and the forgetting of the former troubles.

scenes.scene_name: New Heavens and a New Earth
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The creation of a Jerusalem of joy where weeping is heard no more.
Long life like a tree's, fully enjoying the work of their own hands.

scenes.scene_name: Before They Call, I Will Answer
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The peaceable kingdom where the wolf and lamb feed together on God's holy mountain.
The God no house can contain, who esteems the humble and contrite who tremble at His word.
Hollow sacrifices likened to abominations, judgment chosen for those who would not answer.

scenes.scene_name: The Voice of the LORD Repaying His Enemies
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Comfort to the persecuted who tremble at His word, and the temple-voice of recompense.

scenes.scene_name: Can a Nation Be Born in a Day?
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Zion giving birth before labor — the sudden delivery of her children.
The call to nurse and be satisfied at her comforting breasts.

scenes.scene_name: As a Mother Comforts Her Son
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Peace extended to Zion like a river — 'so will I comfort you.'

scenes.scene_name: The LORD Will Come with Fire
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Joy to His servants but fiery judgment on all flesh by His sword.

scenes.scene_name: I Will Send Survivors to the Nations
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Judgment on the idolaters and the gathering of all nations to see His glory.

scenes.scene_name: Brought as an Offering to the LORD
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The nations bringing Israel's scattered home, some chosen as priests and Levites.

scenes.scene_name: The New Heavens and the New Earth
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The enduring new creation where all flesh worships — and the solemn final image of the rebels' unquenched fire.
